title: Grade 12 Mathematics — Continuity & Differentiability & Applications of Derivatives
description: Continuity and Differentiability and Applications of Derivatives practice questions
subject: mathematics

questions.question: A function f(x) is continuous at x = a if:
questions.explanation: f is continuous at x = a if: (1) f(a) is defined, (2) lim(x→a) f(x) exists, and (3) the limit equals f(a). All three conditions must hold.

questions.question: If f(x) = x² then f'(x) =
questions.explanation: Using the power rule: d/dx(xⁿ) = nxⁿ⁻¹. So d/dx(x²) = 2x.

questions.question: The derivative of sin x is:
questions.explanation: d/dx(sin x) = cos x. This is a standard derivative that must be memorised.

questions.question: The chain rule states that if y = f(g(x)), then dy/dx =
questions.explanation: Chain rule: dy/dx = f'(g(x)) · g'(x). Differentiate the outer function (keeping the inner function unchanged) then multiply by the derivative of the inner function.

questions.question: The second derivative d²y/dx² is used to determine:
questions.explanation: The second derivative measures how the slope (first derivative) is changing — i.e., concavity. f'' > 0 means concave up; f'' < 0 means concave down.

questions.question: At a local maximum point x = c, the necessary condition is:
questions.explanation: At any local extremum (max or min), the derivative f'(c) = 0 (the tangent is horizontal). This is the necessary condition. The sufficient condition uses the sign of f''(c).

questions.question: Rolle's theorem requires: f is continuous on [a, b], differentiable on (a, b), and f(a) = f(b). The conclusion is:
options: There exists c ∈ (a, b) such that f'(c) = 0
f has a maximum at c = (a+b)/2
questions.explanation: Rolle's Theorem: under the given conditions, there exists at least one c in (a, b) where f'(c) = 0 (the tangent is horizontal).

questions.question: If f(x) = eˣ then f'(x) =
questions.explanation: d/dx(eˣ) = eˣ. The exponential function is its own derivative — a unique property.

questions.question: The equation of the tangent to y = x² at x = 2 is:
questions.explanation: At x=2: y=4, slope=f'(2)=4. Tangent: y−4=4(x−2) → y=4x−4.

questions.question: A function is increasing on an interval if:
questions.explanation: A function f is increasing on an interval if f'(x) > 0 for all x in that interval (the function goes up as x increases).

questions.question: The second derivative test says that x = c is a local minimum if:
questions.explanation: Second derivative test: if f'(c) = 0 and f''(c) > 0, then x = c is a local minimum. If f''(c) < 0, it is a local maximum. If f''(c) = 0, the test is inconclusive.

questions.question: The rate of change of area of a circle with respect to its radius r is:
questions.explanation: Area A = πr². dA/dr = 2πr. This is the rate of change of area with respect to radius — which is the circumference.

questions.question: The maximum value of f(x) = −x² + 4x + 3 is:
questions.explanation: f'(x) = −2x + 4 = 0 → x = 2. f(2) = −4 + 8 + 3 = 7. f''(x) = −2 < 0 confirms it is a maximum.

questions.question: Mean Value Theorem guarantees, for f continuous on [a,b] and differentiable on (a,b), that:
options: f has a zero in (a, b)
f has both max and min in (a,b)
questions.explanation: Mean Value Theorem (MVT): there exists c ∈ (a, b) such that f'(c) = [f(b) − f(a)]/(b − a). The instantaneous rate of change equals the average rate of change at some point.

questions.question: The function f(x) = x³ − 3x has a local minimum at:
questions.explanation: f'(x) = 3x² − 3 = 0 → x = ±1. f''(x) = 6x. f''(1) = 6 > 0 → local minimum at x = 1. f''(−1) = −6 < 0 → local maximum at x = −1.
